common.applies_to: Established Hybrid Tea, Floribunda or Grandiflora bush rose (a rose that has passed PKR-SGT-000003); answer to a common question
common.preserved_uncertainty: Protective equipment, cleaning the sprayer, heat and the three statements on what not to combine are each given by one or two sources; they are included as precautions. The evening-only timing rests on one consumer-organisation source. No Australian or US regulator page was read, and which spray types are approved for home gardeners in each country was not established (R-1).

items.text: Read and follow the product label.
In the UK, one source says that following the label is a legal requirement.
Which products are allowed differs by country and changes over time. I couldn't find which spray types are approved in each country, so use only a product labelled for roses where you live.
Don't spray open flowers. One source says to spray only in the evening, once bees are back in their hives.
Wear gloves and safety gear, and clean the sprayer afterwards.
One source says never to spray in the heat of the day.
One source says not to use lime sulphur and copper sprays within two weeks of each other.
One source says never to mix lime sulphur and oil, or spray them together.
One source says not to put oil on a plant that is short of water, or within two weeks of a sulphur spray.
